headline: Last session: Indian markets crashed as Sensex hit 52-week low and Nifty tumbled amid heavy foreign investor selling.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: En-masse selling of Indian stocks by foreign investors
Global rate hikes and rising oil prices sparking outflows
Weak global cues and bond market sell-offs
Longest weekly losing run for benchmark shares in 25 years
whatHappening: Sensex hit a fresh 52-week low during the last trading session
Nifty 50 slipped below the 22,300 mark during intraday deals
Investors lost approximately ₹9.5 lakh crore to ₹10 lakh crore in a single day
The market recorded its eighth consecutive week of losses
summary: On the last trading day, Indian benchmarks suffered a massive sell-off with the Sensex hitting a fresh 52-week low. Foreign investors sold stocks en-masse, wiping out nearly ₹10 lakh crore in investor wealth as Nifty tumbled. The market is closed today for an NSE holiday and will reopen for trading on Monday.
